content.title: About
content.content: Sugar wafer cookies covered in chocolate are light, crisp wafers soaked in a sweet sugar syrup and coated with a thin layer of milk or dark chocolate. They have a delicate sweet flavor, crunchy texture, and a hint of cocoa aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wafer cookies originated in Europe in the 19th century as a light tea-time snack.
The chocolate coating often contains small amounts of emulsifiers to ensure an even layer.
Sugar wafers can be made from wheat or rice flour, affecting their crispness.
In some countries these treats are sold under the brand “Chocolate Wafers” and are considered a traditional confection.
A thin chocolate coating helps preserve the wafer’s crunch by protecting it from moisture.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Sugar and carbohydrates in the wafers provide quick glucose, useful during intense physical activity.

items.title: Contains small amounts of iron
items.content: Chocolate, especially dark, provides iron, which is essential for hemoglobin formation.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Cocoa in the chocolate coating is rich in flavonoids that may protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries with frequent consumption.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wafers are often made from wheat flour, making them unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Milk chocolate allergy
items.content: The chocolate coating may contain milk proteins that can trigger allergic reactions in some individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The cookie can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, added to ice cream, yogurt, or used in dessert compositions. For a softer taste, gently warm in the microwave so the chocolate slightly melts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cookies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer storage, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent the chocolate coating from melting.
